svg.title: The benchmark decentralizes — from one public Index number to a per-workload custom benchmark with cost-per-task and time-per-task
svg.desc: A left-to-right comparison. On the left, "The public Intelligence Index" reports a single quality number — Qwen3.8-27B at 52 — the same fixed workload for everyone; a caution below notes the number hides cost, because producing that score took 160 million output tokens, about 3.7 times the class median, costing 666 dollars and 92 cents to run. A central arrow points to Optima, Artificial Analysis's new custom-benchmark platform launched August 13, fed by four inputs: your own files, agent traces imported from Arize, Braintrust or Langfuse, a coding environment, or a plain-text description of your use case. On the right, Optima reports three numbers on your own workload rather than one: Quality, Cost per Task, and Time per Task — and surfaces an equally good model at up to ten times lower cost or time per task. Along the bottom, an amber dashed band marks the closed ceiling, frozen for a seventh straight brief: Claude Opus 5 at 63 and still number one and uncut, Fable 5 at 62, GPT-5.6 Sol at 61, Grok 4.6 at 60.9, with no Index-64 model, no flagship price cut since July 24, and no new model shipped in the August 19 to 20 window.
svg.text: When the models stop moving, the benchmark does — the Index decentralizes
Aug 19–20 window · no new model, 7th frozen-ceiling brief · the move is a measurement TOOL: Artificial Analysis Optima (launched Aug 13)

The through-line, 3rd window running: the top of the map is frozen, so the motion moves DOWNSTREAM of the models —
first an outside number for one open model (Aug 17), then for another + the meter changing hands (Aug 19), now the
measurement itself decentralizes: one public Index → a benchmark anyone builds on their own data, with cost & time per task.
Optima launched Aug 13; the Aug-18 and Aug-19 briefs missed it — picked up now as it surfaced via coverage/adoption and resolves Aug-18's "price the verbosity" watch-item.
